data.ruling:
The datasheet verifier's refutation stands. The stock verifier raised no refutation and failed no check.

The requirement is the R3 row (Research.md@e13f5f6:281): the external module is qualified for "safe operating area during turn-off". V48 (Research.md@e13f5f6:608, owner answer) sets the current it must open at 600 A on the external path. P2 of FU-A3 turned that into a requirement: 600 A opened without avalanche, at a turn-off rate of 17.8 A/us or less. At that rate the turn-off lasts 34 us, and for all of it the MOSFETs run in their linear (saturation) region against up to 85 V.

The shortlist passes the part on one assumption: the 600 A divides equally over 5 modules in parallel, 120 A each, and 120 A is under the 100 us line of Fig. 14. The datasheet states no current division. With a common gate drive in the linear region, each module's current is set by its own VGS minus VGS(th). The datasheet gives VGS(th) from 1.8 V to 4.3 V, a spread of 2.5 V, at gfs 270 S typ. Fig. 5 shows the 25 degC transfer curve rising from about 20 A to about 100 A over roughly 0.5 V of VGS. So at the gate voltage where the 5 modules carry 600 A together, a module at the low end of VGS(th) can carry several hundred amperes while a module at the high end carries almost none. Fig. 5 also shows that at a given VGS in this range, a hotter module carries more current: the 125 degC and 150 degC curves lie left of the 25 degC curve. The threshold also falls by 9.2 mV/degC. Both push more current into the module already carrying the most.

One module's allowance at 85 V is the 100 us line, 160 A to 169 A. Fig. 14 has no line shorter than 100 us. The datasheet therefore does not show the 34 us turn-off of 600 A inside the safe operating area it states. The check "safe operating area and temperature rise" does not pass on datasheet figures.

The same ground applies to VS-FC420SA10, whose margin was smaller: 136 A against 120 A. The larger 100 us allowance of this part, 165 A (1.37 times 120 A), does not close the gap. The datasheet's VGS(th) spread allows a far larger imbalance than 1.37 to 1.

Every other figure re-read agrees with both verifiers: VDSS and V(BR)DSS 200 V, ID 287 A at 25 degC and 219 A at 90 degC, IDM 680 A, RDS(on) 4.7 mOhm max, RthJC 0.16 degC/W, VGS +/-20 V, IDSS 10 uA max, and the same SOT-227 pinout.

Scope is function, for three reasons:
- The failure comes from this function's V48 current of 600 A and from the 5-module parallel arrangement P2 chose for it.
- Nothing about the part itself fails. Digi-Key reads Active, with discontinued false and end_of_life false. The maker is Vishay, on list S1. The part is off the board, so it has no LCSC number.
- The Vishay product page body has no lifecycle text. The Lifecycle check records that as not read and reports it to the owner; it is not a fail.

A design that bounds each module's current during turn-off could be qualified again: for example, per-module ballast, or a turn-off fast enough to stay under a stated short-pulse line. No such design is in the record.
data.evidence:
VS-FC270SA20 datasheet, Revision 08-Jan-2021, document 96103.

Page 2, electrical characteristics:
- VGS(th) 1.8 V min, 3.16 V typ, 4.3 V max (VDS = VGS, ID 1.0 mA).
- gfs 270 S typ (VDS 15 V, ID 100 A).
- Threshold temperature coefficient 9.2 mV/degC typ, 25 to 125 degC. Fig. 6 shows the threshold falling with temperature.
- RthJC 0.16 degC/W max; RthCS 0.1 degC/W typ.
- VDSS 200 V; ID 287 A at TC 25 degC, 219 A at TC 90 degC; IDM 680 A; RDS(on) 3.3 mOhm typ, 4.7 mOhm max at VGS 10 V, ID 200 A; VGS +/-20 V; IDSS 10 uA max.

Page 3, Fig. 5 (typical transfer characteristics, VDS 20 V):
- The 25 degC curve rises from about 20 A near VGS 4.2 V to about 100 A near 4.75 V.
- The 125 degC and 150 degC curves sit left of it, crossing 20 A near 3.4 V and 3.3 V.
- So at a fixed VGS below the crossing point, a hotter module conducts more.

Page 5, Fig. 14 (TA 25 degC, TJ 125 degC, single pulse), rendered at 600 dpi:
- Plot frame: x from 0.1 V at px 1836 to 1000 V at px 3140; y from 1000 A at px 2775 to 0.1 A at px 3890.
- The column at 85 V is px 2791. There the 100 us line spans px 2985 to 3001, which is 169 A to 160 A, centre 165 A.
- The 500 us line is at about 92 A and the 1 ms line at about 62 A.
- The figure has no 10 us or 30 us line.

Requirement sources:
- R3 row, Research.md@e13f5f6:281: "safe operating area during turn-off".
- V48, Research.md@e13f5f6:608: 600 A external at a 300 A path (owner, 2026-09-28).
- FU-A3 P2 record, scratch/FU-A3/P2-R3/return.json: required "600 A ... opened without avalanche: the turn-off rate held at or below 17.8 A/us". Its datasheet column for the rank-1 part reads "120 A each over 5; at 17.8 A/us the 600 A turn-off takes 34 us, inside the 100 us SOA line". Its placements basis reads "5 keep each at 120 A of the 600 A of V48".
